newsitem.title: USA: Kansas planting progress slowed by wet fields.
newsitem.headline: Kansas planting progress slowed by wet fields.

text.p: Wet fields helped slow or halt planting during in Kansas during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.

Wheat condition improved and was rated 11 percent excellent, 49 good, 29 fair, nine poor and two percent very poor. The crop was 98 percent headed, compared with 97 last year and 98 percent for the five-year average.
Sorghum was 45 percent planted, lagging last year but ahead of the five-year average of 35 percent. Soybeans were 67 percent seeded, ahead of the average of 41 percent.
Corn condition also improved and was rated 10 percent excellent, 71 percent good, 18 percent fair, one percent poor and nil very poor.

"Russian wheat aphids, weevils and chinch bugs have been reported in wheat, and cutworms in alfalfa fields. Infestations were mostly light," the report said. "Diseases reported are wheat streak mosaic, barley yellow dwarf and leaf rust, causing light to moderate damage."
Pasture was rated six percent excellent, 63 good, 26 fair and five percent poor.
Topsoil moisture was two percent very short, 13 percent short, 70 percent adequate and 15 percent surplus.
